passage.text: Therapists can sometimes get lost in the therapeutic process. When this happens, they need to stop and consult their maps in order to regain orientation. In clinical situations, this means that therapists must temporarily withdraw and allow themselves time to reflect. This pause enables the therapeutic situation to become meaningful to them. They can then give a name to this meaning, which constitutes a diagnosis. During this period, therapists consciously and temporarily shift their focus away from the client and the relationship. Instead, they direct their attention toward describing the meaning of the situation, which represents a "third" party in the process.

source.title: Article Aesthetic Diagnosis in Gestalt Therapy
